1.why: Support-the-hypothesis items reward the asymmetric result; the vowel/consonant contrast is the point and A is the only clean asymmetry favoring vowels.

2.why: Only D removes the risk-avoidance correlation itself; the others add or are irrelevant to the mechanism.

3.why: Direct anatomical evidence (heat-shedding vasculature) beats the merely circumstantial climate option D; A and C point at display instead.

4.why: Stem pre-states 'charter not agriculture', and A is the only option that isolates exactly that contrast.

5.why: Hedged middle-ground option; the other three are absolutes ('at all', 'only', 'unimpeded').

6.why: Main-idea key is the qualified corrective ('gradual and deliberate, not a single catastrophe'); others are overstated.

7.why: Classic myth-debunking passage; C is the corrective statement, B is the myth, A and D are supporting details.

8.why: Only B is a control that rules out the skeptics' alternative (visual flow) while leaving step count intact.

9.why: Data-support keys state the correct direction of the trend; B reverses it, C and D cite no relationship.

10.why: Rhetorical-purpose key is the balanced reframing; A/B concede too much, D overreaches.

11.why: Cross-text keys are narrow and hedged ('do not compel'); B and D are the over-agree/over-reject extremes.

12.why: Purpose key is the meta-level point about publication bias; A, C, D take strong first-order positions.

13.why: Only C actually cites numbers, which 'uses data from the text' items require.

14.why: The standard dark-matter counter is cluster-scale evidence; B is factually false and C contradicts MOND's known success.

15.why: Only D gives both sides of the comparison with figures; B reverses direction, C is one-sided.

16.why: 'A cascade requires a slope' is a metaphor for preconditions; D restates it, others overstate.

17.why: Rivera almost certainly argues drought/famine (D supports it), so the weakener is the warfare-plus-full-granaries evidence.

18.why: Monopsony rebuttal shape: attacks an assumption (perfect competition), not the theory itself; C and D are extremes.

19.why: Main-idea key is the reframing claim ('better understood as X than Y'); B and C are details, D is the rejected view.

20.why: Only D reverses the causal order the proposal needs; A and C are consistent with it.

21.why: Supported-inference key is the modest limiting claim; A, C, D are absolute or over-general.

22.why: Author-attitude keys are partial-credit ('valid for some, wrongly generalized'); D is the too-absolute trap.

23.why: Only B is a restrained inference; A, C, D are sweeping generalizations.

24.why: Completion key resolves the apparent conflict by scoping the measurement (shallow layer vs total), the classic reconciliation move.
